lead: Dayton plumbing deals with hard aquifer water, cold winters, older homes and basements. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Dayton.
risk: frozen pipes, aging pipes in older homes and basement backups
risk_short: frozen pipes, old pipes and basement backups
why: The Oregon District, St. Anne's Hill and Dayton View have homes from the 1850s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks, clay sewer laterals and lead service lines in some cases.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and in vacant homes. Heavy rain backs water into basements in older neighborhoods.
water: Dayton pumps its water from the Great Miami Buried Valley Aquifer and softens it at the plant. It is moderately hard at the tap.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Ask the city about your service line material.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in the Oregon District, South Park, St. Anne's Hill, Dayton View, Belmont, Patterson Park, Huffman and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits in Dayton are handled by the local building regulation office for your address. The city and county set the rules for home plumbing work.

faq.a: The aquifer water is hard, and Dayton softens it at the plant. It is moderately hard at the tap, so a yearly water heater flush still helps.
